duration_s_provenance: MEASURED, not asserted: the wall time of results/exp5866_corrigendum_20260727/build.py, which re-reads exp5866's artifact, its raw fixprice.json rows, ops/known-issues.md, results/kaggle_env_probe.json and the submission kernel metadata, and RE-DERIVES both corrections from them. It is small because this is an aggregation pass over persisted objects, not a measurement -- but a hard 0.0 would mean the duration was never measured at all, which is why adversarial_verify.py correctly refused the hand-written first draft. The corrected claims' ORIGINAL measurement cost belongs to exp5866, not here.
why_a_new_artifact_and_not_an_edit: CLAUDE.md never-prune: a committed artifact is a historical record and is not rewritten. Corrections are published as a NEW artifact that cites the original by sha256, so both the original claim and its correction remain readable and the diff between them is auditable.

corrects.what_is_NOT_being_corrected: exp5866's headline conclusions all stand: the VRAM fit (max error 0.19%), the mode A/B/C taxonomy, the finding that context is the cheap axis (~0.025 MiB/cell vs ~207 MiB/slot), and the recommendation to raise n_ctx to 81920. Both corrections below are to SUPPORTING PROSE, and neither changes a number in the fit or the recommendation.

corrections.claim_as_published: PASS at K=4 AND at K=6 (queueing safe). Every request got its FULL 4096-token budget (stop=limit at gen==max_tokens = the intended n_predict budget, NOT pool exhaustion). No 500s, no deaths.
corrections.what_the_raw_rows_actually_say: In the K=6 cell (fixprice.json candidates[0].cells[1]), requests 0-3 returned generated_tokens=4096 with stop_type='limit', but requests 4 and 5 returned 898 and 877 tokens with stop_type='eos' and truncated=false -- a NATURAL finish, not the budget. So 4 of 6 hit the budget and 2 of 6 stopped early on their own.
corrections.why_it_matters: The two queued requests are exactly the ones that test what happens PAST the slot count. Because they finished naturally at ~900 tokens they never asked the pool for their full 4096, so the worst case at K>K_cap was NOT exercised by the evidence offered for the 'queueing safe' claim. The claim rested on rows that did not test it.
corrections.is_the_underlying_claim_true: YES -- verified this session with the evidence the original claim lacked. See k6_forced_full_budget_recheck: K=6 against a fresh n_ctx=81920 server with ignore_eos forcing every request to its full 4096-token budget gave 6/6 HTTP 200, 6/6 at the full budget, 0 truncated, 0 errors, server healthy after. So the CLAIM holds and the published EVIDENCE did not support it -- two different statements, and only the second is the defect.
corrections.corrected_text: PASS at K=4, and PASS at K=6 with the caveat that in the ORIGINAL K=6 cell only 4 of 6 requests reached the 4096-token budget (stop_type='limit'); the two QUEUED requests finished naturally at 898 and 877 tokens (stop_type='eos', truncated=false), so that cell did not exercise the worst case. A separate forced-full-budget run (ignore_eos) is the evidence that does.

corrections.claim_as_published: our scored kernel requests machine_shape NvidiaL4 (scripts/kaggle/submission_kernel/kernel-metadata.json); the 96GB RTX PRO 6000 is a COMPETITOR's request; the only nvidia-smi read this project holds (results/kaggle_env_probe.json -> P100 16GB) is from a different kernel with no machine_shape
corrections.what_the_repository_record_actually_says: ops/known-issues.md lines 2705-2712 record that Kaggle switched the ARC-AGI-3 competition's ACCELERATOR POOL from H100 to `g4-standard-48` on 2026-05-07, per Kaggle staff posts (threads 697720/697944), and that Google Cloud's machine-type docs identify g4-standard-48 as one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition with 96GB GDDR7. A competitor's scored notebook running Gemma-4-31B on 'RTX Pro 6000' is cited there as CORROBORATION of the pool change, not as the source of the claim.
corrections.why_it_matters: 'A competitor's request' implies one entrant chose an unusual machine. The record describes a pool-level change affecting the competition. Getting this backwards understates how loose the scored VRAM envelope may actually be -- which is the exact question the parent lane was asked to establish rather than assume.
corrections.is_the_conservative_sizing_still_correct: YES. exp5866's UNVERIFIED_EXTRAPOLATION status and its decision to size against the 16GB class are correct and well-supported, and the labelling is present in all three of the lane's artifacts. The only direct nvidia-smi read this project holds from any Kaggle kernel is a Tesla P100-PCIE-16GB (results/kaggle_env_probe.json, verified this session), from a kernel with no machine_shape. Whether the pool or the kernel's requested machine_shape governs a scored ARC run is unconfirmed.
corrections.corrected_text: Kaggle moved the ARC-AGI-3 competition accelerator pool to g4-standard-48 (one RTX PRO 6000, 96GB) on 2026-05-07 per Kaggle staff posts; our submission kernel requests machine_shape NvidiaL4; whether the requested shape or the pool governs the scored run is UNCONFIRMED; the only direct read we hold is a 16GB P100 from a different kernel. Status remains UNVERIFIED_EXTRAPOLATION and the conservative 16GB-class sizing stands.

k6_forced_full_budget_recheck.status: PENDING -- not measured at the time of this build
k6_forced_full_budget_recheck.what_it_must_do: K=6 concurrent requests against a fresh n_ctx=81920 llama-server on GPU 1, each with ignore_eos so every request is FORCED to consume its full 4096-token budget. That is the worst case the original K=6 cell did not exercise. PASS = 6/6 HTTP 200, generated_tokens==4096 on all six, truncated=false, server healthy after.
k6_forced_full_budget_recheck.why_it_is_not_filled_in_here: The GPU 1 card was occupied by this session's own first-win measurement arm for the whole build window, and running the probe against that arm's server would have contended with a live measurement. Left explicitly PENDING rather than filled from the review's reported numbers: a corrigendum that copies an unverified number is the failure mode it exists to correct.

corrects.sha256.principle: A corrigendum that does not pin the exact bytes it corrects cannot be checked later: the original could change and the correction would silently attach to a different claim.

corrections[].what_the_raw_rows_actually.principle: READ, DO NOT MODEL. Each correction is stated against the persisted raw object (fixprice.json, ops/known-issues.md), not against a reconstruction of what the artifact should have contained. Two reconstructions agreeing with each other is not evidence about the system.

corrections[].is_the_underlying_claim_tr.principle: Separating 'the claim is wrong' from 'the evidence offered for it was wrong' prevents a correction from retracting a true finding, and names what still needs measuring.

duration_s.principle: An analyser pass over persisted rows is aggregation, not measurement; publishing its own seconds as a measurement cost is the exact error this project made when it reported an 8-second analyser clock as a 2.54-hour measurement.

what_this_corrigendum_does_NOT_do: It does not rewrite results/experiment_5866_generator_concurrency_vram_envelope.json, does not change any number in that artifact's VRAM fit, and does not retract its recommendation to raise n_ctx to 81920. It also does not settle whether exp5866's K=6 'queueing safe' CLAIM is true -- see k6_forced_full_budget_recheck, which is PENDING.
falsifiability_witness_could_have_found_: YES -- and this is the falsifiability witness. Neither correction is forced. C1's builder counts stop_type=='limit' vs 'eos' in the raw K=6 rows: had all six been 'limit', n_finished_naturally_stop_type_eos would be 0 and C1 would have no subject. C2's builder regex-searches ops/known-issues.md for a POOL-level accelerator change: had the record instead described a competitor's machine choice, known_issues_records_a_POOL_level_change would be False and C2 would have no subject. Both conjuncts are computed from the objects, not asserted, so this corrigendum could have come back empty.
